import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_48/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_48/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_48/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_48/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_48/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_48/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_48/training_6.csv"
]

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and types are correct
    # Target schema: ['nombre': string, 'n_concursados': int, 'n_aprobados': int, 'año': int]
    # Convert columns to correct types explicitly
    df = df[['nombre', 'n_concursados', 'n_aprobados', 'año']].copy()
    df['nombre'] = df['nombre'].astype(str)
    df['n_concursados'] = pd.to_numeric(df['n_concursados'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)
    df['n_aprobados'] = pd.to_numeric(df['n_aprobados'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)
    df['año'] = pd.to_numeric(df['año'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target,
# we can concatenate (union) all source tables vertically.
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# The prompt does not specify any aggregation or filtering,
# and the target examples show no aggregation or grouping,
# so we keep all rows as is.

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_48/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
